message: The nonlinear formulas of response 'y' depend on each other in a cycle, so no order computes them: a, b1, mu. A parameter's body cannot name a parameter whose own body names it back (nor itself)
The nonlinear formulas of response 'y' depend on each other in a cycle, so no order computes them: a, mu. A parameter's body cannot name a parameter whose own body names it back (nor itself)
se.fit is not supported for the nonlinear predictor yet; request the nonlinear parameters (dpar = 'a', ...) instead

conditional_effects() cannot put a wald band on a nonlinear predictor: predict() has no standard error for it. Use band = \boot\", which refits instead of differentiating, method = \"predict\", whose band is a quantile of simulated responses, or display one nonlinear parameter with dpar = \"a\""
An update formula written as a delta cannot be applied to a nonlinear formula, whose right-hand side is an expression and not a sum of terms. Pass the complete bf(..., nl = TRUE) as `formula`
nlf() takes a two-sided formula naming the parameter on the left: e.g. nlf(sigma ~ a * exp(b * x))

nlf() declares one parameter at a time, and 'a + b' names several. Sharing one nonlinear body would make them the same function of the data, which leaves the model aliased; write one nlf() per parameter
Invalid parameter name 'a.b': names must be alphanumeric and must not contain dots or underscores (they collide with coefficient naming)
nlf() gives 'a' both a nonlinear body and a linear formula; it can have one or the other
nlf() sets 'sigma', which the bf() it is added to already sets
nlf() sets 'sigma', which the bf() it is added to already sets
lf() sets 'sigma', which the bf() it is added to already sets
nlf() does not say which response it belongs to. Put it directly after the bf() it modifies, e.g. bf(y1 ~ x) + nlf(sigma ~ a * z) + bf(y2 ~ x)

nlf(mu ~ ...) gives 'mu' a nonlinear body of its own, which would leave the right-hand side of the bf() it is added to ('x') with nothing to do. Write bf(y ~ 1) and let nlf() define mu, or move those terms into the nlf() body

A nonlinear formula needs at least one nonlinear-parameter formula whose name appears in the model formula. No name in the body of 'sigma' has one, so every name there is read as a data column and nothing is left to estimate; declare the parameters with bf(..., a ~ 1, nl = TRUE), lf(a ~ 1) or nlf()
Nonlinear parameter(s) not used in the model formula or in any nlf() body: shape
Nonlinear parameter(s) 'z' also name columns of the data. The nonlinear formula would use the parameter and ignore the column; rename one of them

Residual correlation terms are not supported in a nonlinear (nl = TRUE) formula; 'ar()' appears in the model body, where it would be evaluated as ordinary R code rather than read as a term. brms reaches the same model through acformula(), which has no analog here
The nonlinear formulas of response 'y' depend on each other in a cycle, so no order computes them: mu, sigma. A parameter's body cannot name a parameter whose own body names it back (nor itself)
